column3: Normalized documents must resolve lookup queries after applying the same ASCII case and whitespace canonicalization used for stored node names.
Equivalent documents built in different physical orders must compare equal and produce the same semantic fingerprint, including duplicate multiplicities and header identity.
Merging must preserve the greater valid multiplicity of each identical edge rather than collapsing duplicate edges to a single occurrence.
Transitive reduction may remove a direct edge only through a path of at least two edges; parallel direct edges are not alternate paths.
Node-selection permutations must produce byte-identical subgraphs by publishing nodes, edges, attributes, and metadata in source-document order.
Changing an existing node's attribute key or value must mark that node changed while retaining precise added and removed attribute counts.
When a graph contains a self-loop and longer cycles, cycle discovery must return the minimal self-loop witness deterministically.
Manifest metadata entries must be sorted by key so equivalent documents produce byte-stable manifests regardless of insertion order.
Successful JSON, DOT, and GraphML exports must begin fresh context epochs and clear stale diagnostics from earlier failed operations.
Add a public operation that turns selected edges into a valid document containing both endpoints, endpoint attributes, shared metadata, and only selected edges.
